issues.detail: Placeholders are used inconsistently: Step 4 sets PLAYLIST_URL="$1" and then quotes the literal string "PLAYLIST_URL" in later commands, and "URL" and "CHANNEL_URL" are never defined, so it is unclear what the reader should substitute.

Error handling is thin: there is no guidance on geo-blocked, private or age-restricted videos, on HTTP 403/429 failures, or on resuming interrupted downloads. Cookie use is mentioned only briefly, and the Step 11 config sets --write-auto-subs and --convert-subs globally without explaining the side effects.

scenarios.name: playlist-mp3-archive-organized
scenarios.rationale: Both include every required flag and mention ffmpeg, but B gives the exact minimal command the rubric describes, while A adds extra options and tag overrides (parse-metadata, thumbnail crop) that go beyond the request and bury the core command in a script.

scenarios.name: capped-quality-video-with-subs
scenarios.rationale: Both list formats with -F, use a height-capped selector with fallback, --merge-output-format mp4, --embed-subs with --sub-langs en and --write-auto-subs, mention --list-subs and ffmpeg; A adds -S ext preference and a manual-ID option (but uses broader 'en.*,en' langs), B adds a JS runtime note and sticks closer to the rubric's exact selector and '--sub-langs en'.

scenarios.name: polite-batch-channel-download
scenarios.rationale: Both use -a, -x --audio-format mp3, --download-archive, --limit-rate, --sleep-interval with --max-sleep-interval, and correctly explain -N is concurrent fragments of a single video; A is more concise and states clearly that sequential is right, while B adds extras (retries, parallel split suggestion) that are useful but slightly contradict its own advice, and both meet all rubric items.
